svg.title: Running economy against load
svg.desc: Line chart of the oxygen cost of running at an unchanged speed as load builds up, one curve per level. Nothing changes for the first 4 km of load; then cost rises and saturates, 63 per cent of the way to its ceiling 12 km later and nearly all of it by 40 km. At 10 km of load the multiplier is 1.04 for a beginner, 1.02 recreational, 1.01 trained and 1.01 elite; at 20 km 1.07, 1.04, 1.03 and 1.02; at 40 km 1.09, 1.05, 1.03 and 1.02; at 80 km 1.09, 1.05, 1.03 and 1.02, against ceilings of 9, 5, 3.5 and 2.5 per cent.
